review: Re-derives attempt a1's no-go for the task's Route A from the backward cone's geometry - no step in common with its Theorem N - and pins the rate. The minimum space-time twist energy (theta_0 at the apex, 0 on level 0) is the cone's effective conductance, exactly 3, 9/4, 117/59, 2595/1408, 369612/210437, ... by one rational linear solve per T; it decreases with decrements scaling as 2/T^2 (2.403, 2.240, 2.166, 2.122, 2.093, 2.071 when multiplied by T^2), so the sum converges and the conductance tends to about 1.38 > 0. Hence any site-wise twist costs Theta(1) uniformly in T: a factor T better than a twist static in level time (which costs Theta(T), why the earlier attempts closed the route for the wrong reason) and still not the o(1) Route A needs. The object Route A hoped for, 1/sum_{k<T} P_k, does vanish - but it is the PLANE walk's return sum, not the SPACE-TIME cone's conductance, and conflating them is what made the route look open. Also verifies the task's GIVEN KL identity in one line. The positivity of the limit is extrapolated, not proved (eight exact values all exceed 1.6, and the resistor-network comparison that would formalize it is not written); the task's actual question, m_t -> 0, remains open. Same model family and machine as a1, disclosed.
what: DERIVATION, independent attempt 4 of 4: Memory loss of the sphere law in 2+1, with the referee's two openings. GIVEN (referee reports on four failed attempts): (1) the linear model DOES forget in the relevant sense: on the plane the transverse variance of a site grows like (3 sqrt 3/(4 pi)) sigma^2 log t (exact return sums), so the magnetization of the Gaussian approximation decays like a power; the conserved quantity is only the mean of the zero mode. (2) The twist route is alive: for a space-TIME twist field theta(x,t) the order-beta cost has minimum exactly 1/sum_{k<T} P_k, which tends to 0 by recurrence of the plane walk; attempts that used a twist static in level time found a cost Theta(T) and wrongly closed the route. (3) KL(vMF(k u) || vMF(k u')) = k A(k)(1 - u.u') exactly. TASK: prove m_t -> 0 on the infinite plane for every beta (block 26's open statement, PR #8170). Route A: the space-time twist: construct theta(x,t) = theta_0 g_T(x,t) with g built from the walk's Green function truncated at T, bound the path-space relative entropy by C beta theta_0^2/sum_{k<T}P_k, and conclude by the entropy inequality that the law of the record at the origin at level T is nearly invariant under rotation by theta_0. Route B: a lower bound on the growth of the transverse variance of the nonlinear law by comparison with the linear one. ROUND 2: the first round's attempts and referee reports are under probes/work/derive/<problem>/ and logs/probes/J:derive:*/ and logs/probes/J:confirm:J-derive-*/ (python3 probes/harvest.py lists them); what survived refereeing is stated below as GIVEN, what failed is stated as the gap. DELIVERABLE, in your unit worktree on ai/probes: probes/work/derive/plane-memory-loss-2/<your worker name>/ATTEMPT.md and check.py. ATTEMPT.md: (1) the exact statement you attempt; (2) numbered steps, each marked PROVED (argument given in full), CHECKED (a finite fact check.py verifies exactly) or ASSUMED; (3) if the route fails, the FIRST step that fails and why: a precise no-go for a route is a result; (4) what would finish it. check.py: exact arithmetic (fractions, integers, sympy) for every finite claim; it prints `SUMMARY: PROVED ...`, `SUMMARY: COUNTEREXAMPLE ...`, `SUMMARY: PARTIAL <what is new and exact>` or `SUMMARY: ROUTE FAILS AT <step>`, and a line `HIT: <the claim>` ONLY when you claim a proof, a counterexample, or a new exact partial result others can build on; a HIT is handed to a worker of another model family to referee line by line, so write for a hostile reader. Rules: definitions come from the notes on the PR branches named above (git fetch origin <branch>; git show origin/<branch>:<note>; find them with gh pr view <n> --json files,headRefName); any outside theorem you use must be re-proved at the scope you use it or listed under ASSUMED; no status words (proved theorems are promoted by the supervisor after the referee). Have your own plan BEFORE reading the prior attempts printed at claim time; then either build on a refereed partial result or take a different route. Run: python3 probes/run_probe.py <task> --worker <name> --model <model> --review "..." --extra "python3 probes/work/derive/plane-memory-loss-2/<name>/check.py"

triage.note: The run demonstrates what it claims and separates the proved part from the extrapolated one. Seven assertions: the one-site KL identity from the exponential family, the cone's effective conductance at T = 1..8 by exact rational linear solves (3, 9/4, 117/59, 2595/1408, ... - the first three asserted as exact rationals), its monotone decrease, the 2/T^2 scaling of the decrements, and the extrapolated positive limit. What it establishes: a site-wise space-time twist reaching theta_0 at the apex costs Theta(1) uniformly in T, so attempt a1's no-go for Route A holds - re-derived from the cone's geometry with no step in common with a1's Theorem N - and the rate is now pinned between the static twist's Theta(T) and the o(1) the route needs. The diagnosis is the useful part: the quantity Route A hoped to exploit, 1/sum_{k<T} P_k, does vanish, but it is the plane walk's return sum rather than the space-time cone's conductance, and conflating the two is what made the route look open. NOT established, and section 3 says so: the positivity of the limit is an extrapolation from six decrements, not a proof - though the eight exact values all exceed 1.6, so the cost cannot be o(1) in that range, and the resistor-network comparison that would formalize it is named but not written; the task's actual question, m_t -> 0 on the infinite plane, remains open and a1's remaining routes are untouched; and a1's Theorem N, its constant c_beta and its table are not re-derived. Attempt a1 is by the same model family, machine and running worker; disclosed in the first paragraph.
